terminal_record.description_short: The supplied record alleges Patel ordered journalist arrests over leaked documents; the event, date, charges, and response remain unverified.
terminal_record.description_medium: The supplied record alleges that FBI Director Kash Patel ordered investigative journalists arrested and charged under the Espionage Act in August 2025 over leaked government material. It says press-freedom organizations condemned the alleged arrests. The packet identifies no journalists, charging record, or organization statement, and does not verify the supplied August 7 date. This is internal allegation copy, not a verified account.
terminal_record.description_long: An earlier Trump Files entry alleges that, in August 2025, FBI Director Kash Patel directed the arrest of several prominent journalists who were investigating alleged corruption in the administration. It says the journalists were charged under the Espionage Act because they possessed leaked government documents described as detailing financial improprieties. The entry also says press-freedom organizations condemned the arrests as an assault on the First Amendment. These details remain claims from the supplied entry: it does not identify the journalists or organizations, name the documents, or provide an arrest or charging record. The supplied August 7 date is also unverified. This internal draft records the allegation as given and does not assert that arrests, charges, or an order occurred. It does not establish Patel’s role, the source or contents of any leak, or any response by a named organization. The alleged event remains unresolved and is not eligible for publication as fact.

terminal_record.title: Supplied Allegation of FBI Leak Probes Targeting Critical Journalists
terminal_record.description_short: The supplied entry alleges that February 2025 FBI leak probes targeted journalists for critical Trump coverage; the action and motive remain unverified.
terminal_record.description_medium: The supplied entry alleges that the FBI opened leak investigations in February 2025 against journalists and outlets critical of Donald Trump. It says the probes sought sources behind coverage of the Russia investigation, January 6, and Trump’s business dealings, and alleges a chilling effect. The FBI biography supports Patel’s February 20 start date only; it does not establish these probes, their targets, or a retaliatory motive.
terminal_record.description_long: An existing Trump Files entry alleges that the FBI opened leak investigations in February 2025 targeting journalists and news organizations whose reporting criticized Donald Trump. It says the probes sought government sources behind coverage of the Russia investigation, January 6, and Trump’s business dealings, and characterizes the alleged target as critical coverage rather than a specific disclosure. The entry also attributes to press-freedom organizations a condemnation of the action and describes an alleged chilling effect on reporting. The packet does not establish that those investigations occurred or that criticism motivated them. Its February 1 date is a supplied placeholder, not a verified event date. The official FBI biography included in the packet states Patel became director on February 20, 2025; this verifies his start date alone and does not connect him to a probe. This internal draft keeps the asserted action, motive, dates, and reactions explicitly unverified. It does not merge the claim with other March, April, or August records that describe separate alleged events.

terminal_record.description_medium: The supplied record alleges that Trump called immigrants “not human beings” at a July 5, 2019 Cincinnati rally and also attributes “invaded” to that event. The prior review says it could not verify the quote at that rally and flags a possible conflation with a separate May 2018 MS-13 remark. The packet supplies no source excerpts, so the 2019 wording and surrounding claims remain unverified.
terminal_record.description_long: The frozen Trump Files entry alleges that Donald Trump used the phrase “not human beings” about immigrants at a July 5, 2019 rally in Cincinnati, Ohio. It also attributes the word “invaded” to that occasion and frames both phrases as part of a broader pattern of dehumanizing immigration rhetoric. The supplied entry connects the alleged language with claims about scholarship on mass violence, a response by human-rights organizations, immigration raids, and family separation. The packet’s prior review could not verify that the quoted phrase was spoken at the Cincinnati rally and raised a possible conflation with a separate May 2018 MS-13 remark. That review does not establish what was said at either event. This internal draft therefore records the 2019 attribution as an allegation, keeps the 2018 remark separate, and treats the claimed scholarly and organizational reactions and policy links as unverified. The date and exact audience context remain unconfirmed; no connection between these claims is asserted as fact.
